name: Sea buckthorn (Hippophae rhamnoides) fruit and berries
short: Berry oil, a different form, reduced platelet aggregation in 12 healthy men. Fruit extract capsules in 90 adults: no adverse events reported. Fruit adverse-event reports exist, none listed as serious.
text: Fruit and berries by mouth: in a 28-day randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 90 adults with chronic idiopathic constipation, no adverse events or use of rescue treatments were reported with sea buckthorn fruit extract capsules. The abstract of a placebo-controlled trial in 254 healthy volunteers taking a sea buckthorn berry product (233 completed) reports no adverse-event data. A 2024 systematic review of published adverse-event reports after eating medicinal and edible fruits found reports for Hippophae fructus (sea buckthorn fruit) among 12 fruits; overall the 97 adverse events were mainly gastrointestinal, then allergic and neuropsychiatric, and sea buckthorn was not among the fruits listed with serious adverse events; the abstract does not describe sea buckthorn's own events. Platelets: in a small crossover study in 12 healthy men, 4 weeks of sea buckthorn berry oil (a supercritical carbon dioxide extract, a different form from the fruit extract or berries) clearly reduced platelet aggregation; the abstract does not report any bleeding. Psoriasis: the abstract of the placebo-controlled study of sea buckthorn extract on psoriasis lesions does not say how the extract was given and reports no safety data. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
